summary: Chile admits most of Europe, North America, South America and much of Asia-Pacific visa-free for up to 90 days as visitors on a transitory stay permit. Everyone else applies for a consular tourist visa (autorización previa o visa) through Chile's online consular services.

fee.notes: USD 100, paid in the equivalent in Chilean pesos to the Servicio Nacional de Migraciones. Children and adolescents are exempt.

passportValidity.text: Chile's migration service says a transitory stay permit cannot run past the expiry of your passport or travel document, and the UK Foreign Office says your passport should expire after the day you plan to leave Chile. The migration service says nationals of Mercosur countries and Bolivia can enter with a national identity card instead of a passport.

source.name: Servicio Nacional de Migraciones — Permanencia Transitoria

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for entry to Chile. Canada's travel advice tells travellers to get insurance that covers medical evacuation and hospital stays.

source.name: Government of Canada — Travel advice and advisories: Chile

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read states an onward-ticket requirement for visitors to mainland Chile. The UK Foreign Office says visitors to Rapa Nui (Easter Island) must show a return ticket.

source.name: UK FCDO — Chile travel advice (entry requirements)

proofOfFunds.text: Every visitor admitted on a Permanencia Transitoria permit must be able to show the border authority lawful means of support for the stay. No amount is published. Visa applicants must also show their own economic means as part of the consular file.

source.name: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Chile — Información sobre visas para ingresar a Chile

declarations.name: Sworn agricultural declaration (Declaración Jurada SAG)
declarations.submitWindow: From one day before arrival online, or on arrival
declarations.text: Every traveller aged over 18 must complete a sworn declaration for the agricultural service (SAG): it is individual and free, and covers plant and animal products, goods and cash carried in your luggage. SAG's Digital Affidavit for Entry to Chile can be filled in with or without an internet connection from one day before you enter, and is valid only for the arrival date you give; SAG's information page says it can also be made on the form handed out on the flight, and that failing to declare risk products leads to sanctions and fines.

source.name: Servicio Agrícola y Ganadero (SAG) — Digital Affidavit for Entry to Chile (Declaración Jurada), start step

declarations.name: Tarjeta Única Migratoria (TUM)
declarations.text: The PDI border police hand you the Tarjeta Única Migratoria (TUM) when you enter Chile. Keep it for your stay: Chile's migration service lists a valid TUM as the document that lets a visitor on a transitory stay leave the country.

source.name: Servicio Nacional de Migraciones — Guía de ayuda N°5: documentos de viaje para ingresar o salir de Chile

currencyLimits.text: Cash or negotiable instruments of USD 10,000 or more must be declared to customs on arrival and departure.

source.name: Servicio Nacional de Aduanas de Chile — Declaración de Dinero

notes: Chilean law requires every traveller to declare under oath, on the SAG form, any plants, animals, products of plant or animal origin (including handicrafts), agricultural chemicals or animal feed they bring in. Inspectors of the Agricultural and Livestock Service (SAG) check them whatever the quantity, destroy what does not meet the rules, and failing to declare risk products leads to sanctions and fines.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says some small restaurants and stores outside Santiago may not accept credit cards, that US dollars are easily exchanged at banks and official exchange bureaus across the country, and that purchases in US dollars can be made only in certain stores in Santiago.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says pickpocketing, mugging and thefts from vehicles are very common throughout Chile, including in airports, hotels and bus stations. The Government of Canada advises a high degree of caution because of demonstrations, civil unrest and crime, and says armed assaults and robberies have increased in recent years. Both say Chile is in a very active seismic zone where earthquakes and tsunamis can occur.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Chile travel advice: safety and security

idp.text: Chile is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: Declare all food, plants and animal products on the SAG sworn declaration when you enter Chile. The Agricultural and Livestock Service says inspectors check declared goods whatever the quantity, and that failing to declare risk products leads to sanctions and fines.

The Government of Canada says stays on Easter Island (Rapa Nui) are limited to 30 consecutive days, and that to board the flight and on arrival you must show a round-trip ticket and a reservation with accommodation authorised by the local authorities, and complete the Rapa Nui Entry Form. The UK Foreign Office says an invitation letter from the provincial delegation can replace the reservation.
Chile's migration service says nationals of Mercosur countries and Bolivia can enter Chile with a national identity card instead of a passport.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Chile?
faq.answer: Most visitors do not. Citizens of the EU and Schengen states, the UK, Ireland, the US, Canada, Mexico, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Israel, South Africa and most of Latin America enter visa-free for up to 90 days as tourists; Singapore, Malaysian, Macao and Belizean passport holders get 30 days and Indonesians 60. Everyone else applies for a consular tourist visa at a Chilean consulate before traveling.

faq.question: Is there still a reciprocity fee to enter Chile?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states a reciprocity or arrival fee for visa-exempt visitors.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Chile?
faq.answer: Ninety days as a tourist for most visa-free nationalities — 30 days for Singapore, Malaysian, Macao and Belizean passports and 60 for Indonesian ones. One extension of up to a further 90 days can be requested from the Servicio Nacional de Migraciones for a fee of USD 100 (children and adolescents are exempt), and it must be applied for before your current permission expires.

faq.question: Are there extra rules for visiting Easter Island?
faq.answer: Yes. The Government of Canada says stays on Rapa Nui are limited to 30 consecutive days and that you must show a round-trip ticket and an accommodation reservation authorised by the local authorities, and complete the Rapa Nui Entry Form; the UK Foreign Office says an invitation letter from the provincial delegation is accepted instead of the reservation.

faq.question: What is the SAG declaration?
faq.answer: It is the sworn declaration Chilean law requires of every traveller bringing in plants, animals, products of plant or animal origin (including handicrafts), agricultural chemicals or animal feed. It is free and can be filed digitally; SAG inspectors check what you declare, and failing to declare risk products leads to sanctions and fines.

faq.question: Do Venezuelan or Haitian citizens need a visa for Chile?
faq.answer: Yes. Both need a consular tourist visa (autorización previa o visa), applied for through Chile's online consular services.
